title: Domain-Selective Enhancement of Second Harmonic Generation in Monolayer MoS$_2$ via Ferroelectricity-Controlled Photodoping
authors: David Hernández-Pinilla, Line Jelver, María Jesús Martínez-Morillo, César Hernando-Fuente, Miquel Cherta, Guillermo López-Polin, Joel D. Cox, Luisa E. Bausá, Mariola O Ramírez
abstract: Hybrid heterostructures combining two-dimensional semiconductors with ferroelectric materials offer a versatile route to actively control light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. Here, we report all-optical, light-induced domain-selective control of second-harmonic generation (SHG) in monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS$_2$) integrated with periodically poled lithium niobate (LiNbO$_3$). Spatially resolved SHG imaging reveals a pronounced modulation of the nonlinear optical response of monolayer MoS$_2$ governed by the ferroelectric domain pattern of the underlying substrate. A strong SHG contrast is observed between domains of opposite polarization, with a marked dependence on both the excitation wavelength and the incident optical power. The comparison between ferroelectric domains that either enable or do not exhibit light-driven photodoping in the MoS$_2$ monolayer provides a direct assessment of the role of carrier density in the nonlinear optical response. We find that ferroelectric-polarization-controlled photodoping at the MoS$_2$/LiNbO$_3$ interface enhances the effective second-order susceptibility, $χ^2$, producing an increase in SHG intensity of up to ~70% under resonant excitation conditions. Ab initio calculations corroborate that charge doping modifies the electronic band structure of MoS$_2$ and strongly affects $χ^2$ in the resonant regime, providing microscopic support for the experimentally observed modulation. The results highlight the combination of light intensity and ferroelectricity as a powerful knob for band-structure modulation in 2D materials and reconfigurable nonlinear optical responses, opening pathways toward programmable frequency conversion, smart light modulators, and advanced nonlinear photonic functionalities in integrated hybrid platforms.
summary: This study reports on the domain-selective control of Second Harmonic Generation in MoS2 integrated with a ferroelectric LiNbO3 substrate. By exploiting the polarization dependence of the underlying ferroelectric domains, researchers induce photodoping in the MoS2 monolayer. This doping significantly enhances the material's nonlinear susceptibility ($\chi^{(2)}$), enabling programmable and switchable frequency conversion for advanced photonic applications.
main_problem: The study aims to actively control the nonlinear optical response, specifically Second Harmonic Generation (SHG), in monolayer MoS2 by leveraging the ferroelectric domain pattern of an underlying substrate.
main_result: Ferroelectric polarization-controlled photodoping at the MoS2/LiNbO3 interface enhances the effective second-order susceptibility ($\chi^{(2)}$), leading to a significant, up to ~70%, enhancement in SHG intensity between domains of opposite polarization.
method: The research combines all-optical, spatially resolved SHG imaging experiments with ab initio Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations to model the electronic structure and $\chi^{(2)}$ dependence on doping.
model_or_system: The physical system is a hybrid heterostructure combining monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) with periodically poled lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The ferroelectric domains in LiNbO3 induce localized photodoping in the MoS2, which modulates its electronic band structure and nonlinear optical response.
key_observables: SHG intensity modulation correlated with ferroelectric domain polarization ($	ext{P}_{	ext{up}}$ vs. $	ext{P}_{	ext{down}}$), effective second-order susceptibility ($\chi^{(2)}$), and the dependence of SHG on excitation wavelength and fundamental beam power.
important_parameters: The enhancement magnitude (~70%), the role of carrier density (photodoping level, e.g., $\sim 5	imes 10^{14} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$), and the resonant excitation conditions near the C interband transition.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the ferroelectric polarization dictates the local charge doping in MoS2, which in turn governs the magnitude of $\chi^{(2)}$ via band structure modification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spatial SHG mapping showing domain-dependent contrast; spectral analysis shows enhancement near two-photon resonance; and theoretical figures map calculated $\chi^{(2)}$ values based on simulated doping levels.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the platform (MoS2/LiNbO3), presents experimental measurements demonstrating polarization-dependent SHG modulation, attributes this to light-induced photodoping via domain control, and supports these findings with DFT calculations linking doping to $\chi^{(2)}$.
why_interesting: This work provides a clear demonstration of using built-in electric fields (ferroelectricity) combined with external optical pumping (photodoping) as an active knob to engineer the nonlinear optical properties of 2D materials, which is highly relevant for advanced quantum light sources and modulators.
